rows.description: A rich classmate brags and calls my things cheap. I feel ashamed. His words show his insecurity, not my worth; I can walk away and stay close to kinder friends.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, envy, generosity, pity, respect, shame
related mind states: shame, insecurity

rows.description: I cannot afford the class trip and feel embarrassed. It is not my shame to carry. I can talk privately to a teacher, who may find quiet help, and my worth does not depend on money.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, envy, generosity, pity, respect
related mind states: shame, embarrassment

rows.description: The maid or driver at home is treated as lesser by some visitors. Respect means greeting them, saying thank you and remembering they too are somebody's parents.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, envy, generosity, pity, shame
related mind states: gratitude, admiration

rows.description: I see a child begging at a signal and feel a tug in my heart. Wanting to help is good. I can ask my parents about safe ways, like giving food or supporting an organisation.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, generosity, pity, respect, shame
related mind states: trust, empathy

rows.description: A richer friend shares his tiffin and does not make a show of it. I feel grateful and a bit awkward. I can accept warmly and share something of my own in return.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, envy, pity, respect, shame
related mind states: gratitude, embarrassment

rows.description: A classmate is called names for his caste, religion or accent, and I see it. It is not right, and I can feel angry. I can sit with him, and tell a teacher if it continues.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fairness, guilt
related mind states: anger

rows.description: An older relative talks badly about a group and my family nods along. I feel uneasy. I can quietly hold my own view and later ask a trusted elder why they think so.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fairness, guilt
related mind states: anxiety, trust

rows.description: I am told girls should not play cricket or boys should not cry. I feel it is unfair. I can keep doing what I love, find friends who accept me and ask why that rule exists.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fairness, guilt
related mind states: affection, sadness

rows.description: I see the cook being made to drink from a separate glass. I feel confused and sad. Asking my parents about fairness and treating everyone the same is a start.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fairness, guilt, prejudice
related mind states: sadness, confusion

rows.description: Friends want to exclude a child because he is different. I feel afraid to disagree. Staying friendly with him, even quietly, can help him and shows courage.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, guilt, prejudice
related mind states: fear
